text:
Kyle: Quick follow-up from today's AH finance Q&A — collecting practical clarifications about spend approvals, p-cards, and procurement handoffs. Drop specific asks and we'll route them.

Beth: Short answers first, then links/examples.

Anjali: For sandbox infra purchases (trial instances, small cloud spend), what is the default p-card limit for new hires? Any way to get temporary increases?

Beth: Default sandbox p-card limit is $500 for new hires. To get a temporary increase to $2k for an approved project, submit the sandbox spend request form and tag @Beth. Expect 24–48h for routine requests. For any spend > $10k we need a PO.

Tom: If we need to spin up GPUs for a short eval (3–5 days) — can we use a dev credit instead of p-card?

Carlos: We have a limited cloud-credits bucket for research. If it's qualifying work, fill the cloud-credit intake and ops will allocate credits. This avoids p-card.

Anjali: Who owns creating the PO once procurement is approved? engineering or finance?

Beth: Finance creates the PO after you provide: vendor legal name, tax/ACH info, cost center, approver (manager), and the signed vendor onboarding packet. If you include all fields in the first request and mark it 'fast-track', procurement will aim for 48–72h.

Mike: Quick note on laddered or multi‑year commitments — e.g., we commit $X over 3 years with staged payments. How do we do that without killing next FY's flexibility?

Jordan: Legal prefers a master agreement + annual addenda when possible. Finance needs the forecasted commit number and a named budget owner for each fiscal year. That lets us reserve runway while keeping cancellation/rollback language clear.

Anjali: Can we use the same template if the vendor is a small consulting shop (low risk)?

Jordan: Small vendors can use a simplified SOW; still need basic terms (IP, confidentiality, payment). Legal review is typically lighter but still required for any payment > $25k.

Tom: Any exemptions for purchases tied to grants or sponsored research (cloud credits, vendor reimbursements)?

Mike: If it's a grant, we have a program code flow. Finance can code the spend to the grant and bypass p-card if you provide the grant ID and sponsor contact.

Anjali: Also — is there a preapproval button for a 1–2 day emergency invoice so services don't block?

Beth: For true emergencies, include 'EMERGENCY' in the subject to invoices@redwood.com and the approver chain in the email body. We'll triage. Don't use that as a normal path; it's reserved.

Anjali: Can someone drop the sandbox request form + PO template here?

Beth: Links: https://intranet/redwood/forms/sandbox-request and https://intranet/redwood/templates/po-template.docx — use the PO template fields exactly to avoid back-and-forth.

Sarah: For Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pools) procurement: who negotiates the service contract? Is Sales or Finance the lead?

Kyle: For Dedicated we treat it as a service contract. Sales leads negotiation, Finance signs off on payment terms and forecasting. If you want laddered compute commits we need cancellation windows and a named business owner in the contract. Ping @Sarah for the deal-level conversation.

Anjali: Final quick ask — is there an internal checklist for onboarding a vendor that includes SSO, billing, and security signoffs?

Beth: Yes — vendor onboarding checklist is on the intranet (link in #procurement). Steps: onboarding packet -> legal review -> security review (if services access infra) -> finance PO -> SSO provisioning. For expedited cases, mark each step with 'expedite' and include justification.

Invoices Bot: Reminder: send invoices to invoices@redwood.com with PO# in subject. Missing PO -> will be quarantined.

Mike: :thumbsup: great thread. if folks want 1:1s we can schedule office hours next week.

Anjali: Thanks everyone — super helpful.

Beth: We'll follow up with a short FAQ and the templates in #all-hands pinned. :white_check_mark:
